For the time being, at least, Cattermole’s first senior management role is not going at all well. articles.title: Australia v South Africa: international men’s rugby union Test – live
articles.summary: Updates from the Wallabies v Springboks match in Perth. Kick-off at Optus Stadium is 5.45pm local/7.45pm AEST. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. The individual under the most scrutiny today will be Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii.
body: It’s a massive opportunity to challenge a fantastic team that is second to none in the world. An opportunity to challenge ourselves too. We won’t shy away; we’ll take it on. This 80 minutes will be a representation of where we’re at – and who we are.
That’s Wallabies coach Les Kiss, who had a chat with our own Angus Fontaine last week.
“The focus for us is physicality,” puffs Rob Valetini as he makes his way down the tunnel after the warm-up. He also suggested new winger Suaalii would be used as an aerial target.

The Australian camp have been keen to stress this isn’t a demotion but an opportunity to get the powerful runner into the action in areas where he has more room to express himself. Michael Hooper on TV says he expects Suaalii to swing off his wing at times to provide attacking impetus, especially on the counter when he isn’t required to hold width as an aerial target.

articles.title: In playful moments, the USMNT’s new youth movement is already paying off
articles.summary: After a crushing World Cup exit, 11 debutants and two teenage scorers are giving the program renewed verve. Subscribe to our free newsletter for US soccer fans. Follow Guardian Soccer on Instagram and TikTok.
body: The fans who witnessed the United States’ 4-1 thrashing of Peru in Orlando on Saturday did not have to wait long to get their flashbulb moment. It came just four minutes into the match, only moments after 19-year-old Orlando City attacker Justin Ellis headed home the US opener.

Ellis, making his first appearance for the US, sprinted toward the near corner to celebrate, then turned and faced the US supporters in the north end of Inter.co Stadium – a supporters’ section nicknamed “the wall”. Quickly, he was joined by Villarreal defender Alex Freeman, himself an Orlando City product. For a moment, the two former teammates posed arm in arm, gazing up at the home crowd. Then they embraced, laughed, and attempted to run back to the center circle. Gio Reyna, who’d assisted on the goal, shoved him back toward the fans.

“Celebrating that goal with Alex – it was ridiculous,” Ellis told reporters after the match. “He’s like family to me. It was unbelievable … I think Gio also just understood the moment, being back home in front of the wall, it was just super special.”

articles.title: From turgid to thrusting - mixed start for new Scotland
articles.summary: BBC Sport Scotland's Tom English reviews a mixed start to life as Scotland head coach for Sebastien Pocognoli as his side open their Nations League campaign with a goalless draw in Slovenia.
body: For 45 turgid minutes in Slovenia, some in the Tartan Army might have reimagined the Steve Clarke years as a time of plenty, the halcyon era of ambitious football when Scotland were an all-electric thrill-fest.
The opening half of the Sebastien Pocognoli regime was, as expected, disjointed.
It was also, rather unexpectedly, devoid of anything remotely related to what Pocognoli laid out as his non-negotiables - front-foot pressing, high intensity, speed of thought and mind, goal threat.
They had no shot on target and lost so many aerial duels that you stopped counting beyond the half-hour mark. They took 38 minutes to touch the ball in Slovenia's penalty area.

articles.title: Man City? I feel cheated - when do Stoke City get our FA Cup?
articles.summary: BBC Sport columnist Tony Pulis explains what he and all Stoke fans are thinking after Manchester City are found guilty of the majority of the 115 charges they faced.
body: That is what all Stoke City fans have been asking me since the news broke on Friday that Manchester City had been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they have been accused of breaching.
While the process is far from over because Manchester City are expected to appeal, I have to say this verdict and the whole situation has left a very sour taste in my mouth.
Taking my Stoke side to the 2011 FA Cup final was one of the highlights - if not THE highlight - of my 50 years in football as a player and manager.

That day in May will also live long in the memory of all Stoke fans who followed their team to Wembley dreaming that they would win the greatest club cup competition in world football for the first time in their long history.

articles.title: White casts doubt on Fury-Joshua after 24 hours of chaos
articles.summary: There is fresh uncertainty around the proposed Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua fight - after Dana White said he did not know whether it would happen.
body: Two days after the announcement British boxing had waited a decade for, Dana White - the UFC president and Zuffa Boxing chief named as one of the figures promoting Tyson Fury against Anthony Joshua - was asked whether the fight would actually happen.

White was speaking at London's Copper Box on Saturday, where British heavyweight Johnny Fisher beat Michael Pirotton on his Zuffa Boxing debut. But for much of the media in attendance another heavyweight fight dominated the evening.
Asked whether Wednesday's scheduled Fury-Joshua news conference in London would take place, White added: "I have no idea."
On Thursday, Fury and Joshua were officially announced to meet at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December, live globally on Netflix. By Friday, that certainty had unravelled.

articles.title: Raoni Barcelos Delivers Veteran Performance Against Raul Rosas Jr. Before Suffering Scary UFC Vegas 121 Ending
articles.summary: While Raoni Barcelos and Raul Rosas Jr. put an all-time classic at UFC Vegas 121, the scary ending to the bout is what fans are talking about.
body: The UFC Vegas 121 main event delivered an all-timer as Raul Rosas Jr. and Raoni Barcelos went to war for nearly five rounds. What looked like a serious Fight of the Year contender, however, ended in an incredibly scary fashion when the 39-year-old Barcelos appeared to lose consciousness after a takedown in the final round.

The fight was fast from the opening bell, with Rosas Jr. coming out guns blazing. The 21-year-old immediately put pressure on the veteran, throwing combinations and forcing Barcelos to open up his own offense. Rosas landed a clean shot that caught Barcelos’ attention, prompting the Brazilian to shoot for a single-leg. Rosas quickly freed his leg and went straight back to letting his hands go.

Barcelos gradually found his rhythm and began closing the distance. That momentum carried into the second round, where he put together a huge offensive surge and landed nearly 60 significant strikes. Rosas continued pushing forward with crisp boxing, but the veteran absorbed the punishment and kept firing back. Barcelos also mixed in his wrestling, scoring a clean takedown, although Rosas was able to scramble back to his feet.
points: While Raoni Barcelos and Raul Rosas Jr. put an all-time classic at UFC Vegas 121, the scary ending to the bout is what fans are talking about.

articles.title: Alpine to consider what action to take after three-car Colapinto crash
articles.summary: Alpine chief Flavio Briatore says he will take time to "reflect on what course of action should be taken" after Franco Colapinto's "very poor" error caused a three-car collision in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
body: Attempting to make a bold move from 10th place down the inside into Turn One at the first Safety Car restart, Colapinto locked his brakes and hit the side of team-mate Pierre Gasly, who was sent straight into Lando Norris' McLaren on his outside. All three drivers retired.
Gasly had been running a strong seventh at the time and the incident cost Alpine what stood as seven points overall.

With both Alpines and Norris having dropped out ahead of him, Arvid Lindblad instead came through late in the race to finish seventh and stretch Racing Bulls' lead over Alpine in the fight for fifth place in the Constructors' Championship to 15 points with a scheduled eight rounds left.

Speaking in Alpine's official press release after the race, executive advisor Briatore made clear his frustration at Colapinto's driving, for which the Argentine unreservedly apologised, and said they would work out what to do to ensure lessons were learnt to avoid a repeat in future.

articles.title: Adola wins men's Berlin Marathon, Assefa dramatically misses record
articles.summary: Ethiopia's Guye Adola won the men's event at the Berlin Marathon on Sunday, while compatriot Tigst Assefa was victorious in the women's race but failed to set a world record in a dramatic finish.
body: Assefa was comfortably en course to beat Ruth Chepng'etich's record of 2 hours 9 minutes 56 seconds from the 2024 Chicago Marathon.
But in the final kilometres, she was in great distress due to what looked like a muscle injury or cramp, and was even limping.
After crossing the finish line at the Brandenburg Gate in 2:11:04 hours, she immediately went down in pain.
Assefa has previously won the Berlin Marathon in 2022 and 2023, when she set the record at the time of 2:11:53 hours.

articles.title: Wakefield hailed after stunning Wigan: 'No team would have competed!'
articles.summary: Jon Wilkin believes some of the best teams in Super League history would not have beaten Wakefield Trinity on Saturday night, as Daryl Powell's side sealed a huge upset victory against Wigan Warriors to book a spot in the Grand Final.
body: A flurry of second-half tries saw Trinity end Wigan's 16-match winning streak, with the visitors leaving Matt Peet's side stunned by their ferocious pace and power.

Wigan went down to 12 men after 45 minutes, with Adam Keighran being sin-binned for a tip-tackle. Wakefield ruthlessly took advantage, scoring three tries while the Australian five-eighth was off the field.
Wigan did impress in the opening exchanges, matching Wakefield for intensity, with Brad O'Neill breaking the deadlock after a tense first 15 minutes.
But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.

articles.title: 'These things are never over!' - Can Team USA avoid another Medinah upset?
articles.summary: Brandt Snedeker has given a self-critical assessment of his own Presidents Cup captaincy so far, with time quickly running out to avoid an embarrassing defeat for Team USA on home soil.
body: Team USA came into the week as overwhelming favourites to claim a record-extending 11th consecutive victory, in a biennial event where much of the pre-tournament narrative was around whether change was needed to make it more competitive.

Next to no hope had been given to Geoff Ogilvy's International Team, who earned their only Presidents Cup win in 1998 and have lost every edition since a 17-17 tie in 2003, but they are now five points away from completing a seismic shock at Medinah.

A clean sweep in the Friday foursomes gave the visitors a 7-3 advantage heading into Saturday's double session, where the Internationals saw the leaderboard filled with red numbers in both - indicating American leads - before delivering late fightbacks.

The Internationals claimed a share of the spoils in the afternoon foursomes to take a 10.5-7.5 advantage into the Sunday singles, just the fourth time they've led heading into the final day of a Presidents Cup and first experience of it on American soil.
